title: Machine-learning analysis identifies kinematic evidence for a protoplanet in the HD 142666 disk
summary: A machine-learning model identified a strong, localized non-Keplerian gas-motion feature in the protoplanetary disk around HD 142666. Hydrodynamic simulations of a system containing a 5-Jupiter-mass planet at 75 au reproduced the observed kinematic structure; the authors conclude that HD 142666 hosts an embedded planet by current field criteria. The planet is inferred from disk kinematics rather than directly imaged.
ai_technology: EfficientNetV2 and RegNet image classifiers (six channel-count variants), trained on synthetic planet/no-planet disk observations
organization: University of Oxford (J. P. Terry’s repository-listed affiliation); University of Georgia (resource support acknowledged in the paper)

evidence.tested: A machine-learning model identified a strong, localized non-Keplerian gas-motion feature in the protoplanetary disk around HD 142666.
evidence.unknown: The paper’s planet conclusion is an inference from gas kinematics supported by simulations, not a direct image or independent dynamical mass measurement. The models were classifiers, not trained to localize planets, and the 5-Jupiter-mass, 75-au configuration is a simulation that reproduces the observed feature, not a separately measured planet parameter.
evidence.ai_role: The classifiers applied to ALMA data assigned high planet-presence scores and their activation maps highlighted the previously unreported non-Keplerian velocity kink; the authors then used standard hydrodynamic simulations to test whether an embedded planet reproduced that feature.
